newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Nurse emerges as heroine in NZ shotgun massacre.
newsitem.headline: Nurse emerges as heroine in NZ shotgun massacre.

text.p: A pregnant nurse emerged on Monday as a heroine from the weekend shotgun massacre in rural New Zealand which left six people dead and six wounded.
Anna Dawson, 30, helplessly cradled a dying man at the roadside as a killer went on a shooting rampage on Saturday in Raurimu, a small settlement in the central North Island.

Dawson, a nurse at the Taumarunui hospital, came across local man Hendrick Van De Wetering just minutes after he had been shot and the gunman had fled into the adjacent bush, his gunfire still punctuating the morning air.
"I'm feeling still very shocked. I feel really tired, and sad," Dawson said on Monday.
Along with four others, she tried desperately to help the dying "Henk" Van De Wetering, 51, a well known and loved member of the close-knit Raurimu community.
A 22-year-old unemployed man was arrested naked a few hours after the slayings and has been charged with Van de Wetering's murder. Police said more charges are likely to follow.

Stephen Anderson, from Wellington, who authorities have said was a mental health patient, showed no emotion as he appeared barefoot and in police overalls in Taumarunui district court, 34 km (20 miles) from Raurimu, on Sunday. He was remanded in custody to appear in Hamilton District Court on Wednesday.
A psychiatric report was ordered. Family friends said Anderson was diagnosed as schizophrenic last year.
Dawson, mother of one and two-months pregnant, said she didn't think of the danger she was in when she came across the murder scene.
"It's just hitting home with me now, what danger we were in and what's happened to the families in the area and how many people are grieving," she said.
"I suppose I've had some experience with grief and grieving people, but I'm still shocked and really sad about what's happened."
Raurimu is an idyllic small farming and ski resort area nestled in rolling hills beneath Mount Ruapehu, an active volcano.
The murders have left residents stunned and grief-stricken.
"You don't really expect these sorts of things to happen here," Dawson said.
"They're supposed to happen overseas really, aren't they?"
Despite New Zealand's image of tranquillity, before Saturday's killings there had been four mass murders killing 31 people since 1992.
